annotations.annotation_text: Egyptian eschatology "set" on page 297 ("The Night Lessons"): within the children studying the Trivium and Quadrivium, Dolph and Kev drawing geometric diagrams of ALP's body, marginal glosses and footnotes, HCE appears as the dismembered Osiris and ALP as Isis gathering his scattered limbs. Mark Troy's research traces how Joyce embedded the Papyrus of Ani's resurrection liturgy throughout this Age of Heroes passage — the dream-journey through the underworld (Tuat) toward solar rebirth.
sources: Budge, E.A. Wallis. The Book of the Dead (Papyrus of Ani). https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1300
Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: ALP invocation "A.L.P" on page 297 ("The Night Lessons"): Anna Livia Plurabelle, the mother-river personifying the Liffey, surfaces here amid the children studying the Trivium and Quadrivium, Dolph and Kev drawing geometric diagrams of ALP's body, marginal glosses and footnotes. In this Age of Heroes passage, her feminine current of forgiveness and renewal flows through the dream landscape, carrying Dublin's history from source to sea.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "midden" on page 297 ("The Night Lessons"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within the children studying the Trivium and Quadrivium, Dolph and Kev drawing geometric diagrams of ALP's body, marginal glosses and footnotes. During this Age of Heroes phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "dream" on page 297 ("The Night Lessons"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within the children studying the Trivium and Quadrivium, Dolph and Kev drawing geometric diagrams of ALP's body, marginal glosses and footnotes. During this Age of Heroes phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
